description: Dual-render workflow for every 3D design in Helping Hands. For each design, make (a) a three.js web concept render of the intended look and (b) the OpenSCAD part, exported to STL and loaded into the SAME viewer. Render both from the same fixed camera angles (front, side, top, iso, plus exploded) and put the pairs side by side, with a silhouette/overlay diff that highlights where they differ. Write a short 'differences and why' note per design (e.g. a printability constraint, a missing feature, wrong proportions) and the fix list. The OpenSCAD STL is the printable source of truth; the web render is the vision reference, not assumed correct. Show both on the Designs page cards (voice-0c526dc0). Apply it to the gripper generations and the Robot Glove Hand first. Make it one script: render_compare <design>.

results.identified_issue:
Approach: ONE three.js page (cad/compare/viewer.html + viewer.js, three 0.185.1 vendored from ~/Isleo/node_modules) draws both the concept module (<family>/web/gen_NN.js, CAD mm Z-up, returns [{name, object, explode}]) and the STLs from cad/compare/designs.json, using one shared orthographic framing (union bbox of both models), so the panes line up pixel for pixel. Diff = two silhouette render targets + composite shader. IoU per view comes from readRenderTargetPixels.

designs.py is the single registry. It auto-discovers cad/openscad/*/gen_NN_*.scad, and pieces come from export/parts.json (group-filtered) plus export/gen_NN_*.stl. It does the fuzzy match used by design.sh, the URL and render_compare. --export re-exports one generation via OpenSCAD part="parts" echo rows (same as export.py's mesh step, no renders). It was verified byte-identical for gripper gen_01. in_progress = agent/ pebbles with working_on whose id appears in the gen's files, or whose text names the family phrase (folder name minus demo/robot); family mentions mark only the newest gen. After give-to-human clears working_on the badge disappears, which is intended. designs.json is gitignored; every consumer regenerates it first.

render_compare: headless Chrome against `python3 -m http.server`. Chrome intermittently fails dynamic import() under --virtual-time-budget (an in-process ThreadingHTTPServer looked guilty but plain http.server fails too). Fixes: concept files import nothing (helpers come in via build's 2nd arg from cad/compare/shapes.js), the viewer retries the import with a fresh ?t=, and render_compare retries the whole run up to 6x. The PNG comes back as a data URL in #result (labels burnt in via a 2D canvas), so there is no separate screenshot run.

Mac app: RepoDesigns (DesignWorkbench.swift, macOS only) reads GitInfo.repoRoot. It shells `python3 designs.py`, uses FSEventStream on cad/openscad, cad/compare and pebbles/agent (0.4 s debounce, a .scad save means export then reload, anything else means reload), and serves the repo to WKWebView through a custom hhrepo:// scheme handler (no server). Workbench panes share an orbit via webkit message handler 'hh' → CameraLink → hh.setCamera. Live reload keeps the user's camera. URL: AeroURLDelegate routes host 'designs' to RepoDesigns.open(name:), which activates and toggles the window to full screen. Designs tab on the Mac = RepoDesignsScreen when the checkout exists, else the bundled DesignViewerScreen (iOS unchanged).

NOT verified: never built or ran the app (no-build rule). DesignWorkbench.swift typechecks standalone with swiftc against Generated/GitInfo.swift. The HelpingHandsApp/AeroHandPanel edits are small but were not compiled. WKWebView-specific risks: WebGL + import maps + module scripts over a custom scheme (Safari 16.4+ supports import maps); many WebGL contexts if the design count grows (each card = 2 web views). export.py's stale cleanup now skips compare_*.png, otherwise it deleted the sheets. glove_hand/export/*.stl is gitignored by the root *.stl rule (pre-existing), so a fresh checkout needs `designs.py --export glove` first. I re-exported it locally as binary STL. The concepts are my reading of the READMEs, not Jake's vision. Notes in <family>/compare/gen_NN.md say so implicitly via the fix lists.
results.summary: Every design now has a web concept and an OpenSCAD STL render side by side with a diff, and 'work on <design>' opens them live and full screen in the Mac app.
results.detailed_description:
Say "work on gripper" (or "glove hand", "gripper gen 0") and the voice session runs Scripts/design.sh. That opens helpinghands://designs/<name>, and the Mac app comes forward full screen with the three.js concept large on the left and the OpenSCAD STL on the right. Both panes share one camera, so orbiting one moves the other, and there are Front/Side/Top/Iso/Exploded presets plus a Diff toggle (magenta is in the vision only, cyan is in the STL only). The app watches the files: saving a .scad re-exports just that generation's STLs (under a second), and saving a concept redraws.

The Designs tab on the Mac now reads the checkout, not the build. Every design gets a card with its current web and STL renders and an orange "In progress" badge while a claimed pebble is on it, plus a Refresh button (⌘R).

Scripts/render_compare <design> writes the five-view comparison sheet (attached: gripper gen 01) and an overlap table into <family>/compare/gen_NN.md. I wrote the differences-and-why and fix lists for both gripper generations and the glove hand. The concept renders are my reading of the READMEs, so tell me where they miss your vision. I haven't run the app itself (no building here), so once Vigil builds it, try "work on glove hand" and tell me what you see.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey — done. Every 3D design now gets two renders from the same camera angles: the three.js concept of how it should look, and the real OpenSCAD part that prints. A diff highlights where they disagree. Say "work on gripper" and the Mac app opens it full screen with both side by side, updating live as it's edited. Each design also has a short note on what differs, why, and what to fix next.

It must show the CURRENT state, even unfinished and while an agent is editing it: watch the design's files and live-reload both renders on every save. Add a helpinghands://designs/<name> URL plus a script (design.sh <name>) so the voice session opens it deterministically, and have the app list designs by name for fuzzy matching ('gripper', 'glove hand').
